children: Polish copper and silver producer KGHM
posted on Wednesday a third-quarter net profit that surpassed estimates, supported by steep prices of copper and silver but partly offset by rising costs.
Industry surveys place KGHM among top silver producers and among the 10 largest copper miners, and investors watch it closely as a barometer of demand across the metals sector.
• The miner's net profit for the quarter surged to 1.94 billion zlotys from 433 million a year earlier; a Reuters poll of analysts had estimated 1.33 billion

• Revenue rose to 12.04 billion zlotys ($3 billion) from the year-ago 8.32 billion zlotys, despite stable copper production and sales domestically; electrolytic copper production increased 0.5% while copper sales rose 1.1%
• Minerals extraction tax went up 110% over the prior-year period
• "Volatile energy and commodity prices remain a challenge beyond our control, so we are implementing measures to improve cost and operational efficiency," CEO Remigiusz Paszkiewicz said
• Copper prices fell for the fifth consecutive session on Wednesday, reaching their lowest level in more than six months, pressured by a stronger dollar and AI investment concerns
